chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Ayyub, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

If he performs i'tikaf for one day and has not stipulated (a condition for duration), then he may exit and break his i'tikaf. And if he stays for two days and has not stipulated, then he may not exit and break his i'tikaf until three days have passed.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for breaking i'tikaf if no specific duration was stipulated?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the Shia jurisprudential distinction between a 'conditional' i'tikaf (where the worshipper specifies a duration) and an 'unconditional' one. It establishes that while a one-day i'tikaf without a stipulated term can be terminated at any time, a two-day i'tikaf becomes binding for a full three-day period once initiated, reflecting the principle of stability in worship obligations. This ruling is central to the chapter on 'al-Ishtirat' (stipulation), highlighting how intent and specification alter the legal status of the ritual seclusion.
